definition: A typed package `(Z, f, Σ_f, E, A)` comprising carrier, declared lens, induced definability structure, packaging/completion endomap, and audit. Variants may add dynamics or records but must not silently replace these fields.
noncollapse: A theory package is not merely a model description; formation claims require fixed-point and audit records.

definition: The underlying finite state/content domain `Z` on which the package is defined.
noncollapse: Carrier identity, theory identity, and layer identity are distinct.

definition: A declared map/interface `f` specifying what distinctions are available to the package.
noncollapse: A lens may be partial in future VII work, but the existing canonical package does not by itself supply a partial-domain calculus.

definition: `Σ_f`, the family/algebra of distinctions expressible through the declared lens.
noncollapse: Definability is lens-relative; hidden carrier distinctions are not automatically layer facts.

definition: The endomap `E` whose fixed points supply packaged candidates and whose idempotence/defect is audited.
noncollapse: Iterating one fixed idempotent does not generate an open-ended ladder.

definition: The record/check functional `A` and surrounding provenance discipline under which a package or claim is accepted.
noncollapse: Audit is constitutive of admissibility, but SBT is not reducible to audit.

definition: A declared fixed point of completion with its associated formation, record, and audit conditions included in the package.
noncollapse: Fixed-point syntax alone is not sufficient when formation records or audits are absent.

definition: Evidence that a candidate survives the declared packaging/completion operation, exactly or within a declared defect tolerance.
noncollapse: Objecthood is separate from novelty and directionality.

definition: A refinement/new package retains the lower readout and separates at least one lower-indistinguishable pair; equivalently, the new readout does not factor through the old.
noncollapse: Strictness alone does not imply closure, promotion acceptance, endogeny, or drive.

definition: An accepted P6-side audit of time-reversal asymmetry or non-exact affinity that survives the declared observation/protocol conditions.
noncollapse: Route mismatch or holonomy alone is not directionality.

definition: The affinity-carrying, detailed-balance-breaking face of P6 used for honest directionality claims.
noncollapse: It is a specialization of P6, not a seventh role and not a replacement for general audit.

definition: An ordered sequence of closures/packages in which later stages are strictly stronger; open-endedness requires changing or enlarging operators/interfaces rather than repeated application of one idempotent.
noncollapse: Finite fixed interfaces have bounded definability and cannot support an infinite strict ladder.

definition: Behavioral status, verification/certificate, and structural-categorical support are three lossy levels for each primitive role.
noncollapse: Lifts upward require added data and are selected, not unique.

definition: The finite audited typed closure-description domain over which Foundations II proves its scoped exact-six theorem.
noncollapse: Membership does not require all six role projections to be active.

definition: One of exactly six typed slots in a decomposition/exhaustion record; a channel may be inactive, below threshold, collapsed, absent-with-record, or out of scope.
noncollapse: Channel presence is not role activation.

definition: An honestly supported interpretation of raw features as one P-role, carrying threshold, witness, level, evidence, collapse, loss/lift, and nonclaim data.
noncollapse: A FATCD description may activate none, some, or all six channels.

definition: Within FATCD and an explicit recognition hypothesis, every admissible description has an existential, non-unique decomposition/exhaustion record with six role channels and no required seventh irreducible role in the covered scope.
noncollapse: Not a universal algebra, uniqueness theorem, empirical realization, or claim that every description activates all six.

definition: The finite audited typed interaction record/calculus carrying packages, instruments, profiles, witnesses, updates, defects, judgments, statuses, gates, dependencies, audits, visibility, sources, nonclaims, and model realizations.
noncollapse: It is not a category, algebra, or closure operator. The body’s 19-field declaration controls an inconsistent 16-field appendix shorthand.

definition: A typed judgment `P_i ← P_j` in which actor `P_i` consumes informant witness data from `P_j` through a typed update under package, profile, visibility, threshold, defect, and audit records.
noncollapse: Pair order matters; a cell action does not make the unordered pair observable real.

definition: A separate unordered-pair judgment with joint source-of-truth and branch-compatibility obligations.
noncollapse: A real/action cell does not imply a real pair observable; fallback/proxy sources are at most provisional unless explicitly upgraded.

definition: A finite typed bridge from a source package to a target package, classified only after required gates and audit records are present.
noncollapse: Strict bridge data is separate from target closure and drive.

definition: A typed classifier codomain tied to one judgment family; BirdInt keeps Role, Cell, Pair, Promotion, Claim, Gate, and Square statuses separate.
noncollapse: Status values cannot be transported between families by name resemblance.

definition: The coarsest quotient carrying the observations declared by an instrument/interface.
noncollapse: Layer claims must factor through the access quotient unless extra apparatus is declared.

definition: An exact current-layer claim must be constant on access fibers and therefore factor through the access quotient.
noncollapse: A true carrier fact may still be inadmissible as a current-layer claim.

definition: A strict visible distinction cannot be produced from the existing access quotient alone; additional memory, bridge, residual budget, scope, or calibration data must be declared.
noncollapse: This is adjacent to, but does not yet settle, a VII no-free-access theorem.

definition: The split-pair set of lower-equivalent points whose transported/readout values disagree; emptiness is equivalent to descent.
noncollapse: Canonical repairs are source refinement or minimal target coarsening.

definition: A public quotient universal across declared access quotients; objectivity means a readout is common across accesses and determined by that public quotient.
noncollapse: Common source and common quotient are not the same as common access or a strict join.

definition: A theory/package refining multiple lower packages under declared bridge conditions.
noncollapse: A common refinement is not automatically an interaction, strict join, or shared-access certificate.

definition: A candidate law is lawful at a layer exactly when it factors through the available access quotient.
noncollapse: Application of a named law still requires a bridge from application objects to theorem objects.

definition: A typed, source-located, auditable association between events/claims and provenance; F20 supplies formed-record discipline.
noncollapse: Passive logs and unowned analyst annotations need not be formed records.

definition: For quotients on a common carrier, the coarsest quotient refining both. It supplies distinctions but not source, cost, utility, access, or interaction admissibility.
noncollapse: Do not confuse this vertical/common-carrier operation with the desired VII join between formed theories.

definition: Declared reduction in closure deficit from current quotient to predictive baseline, or a certified residual surrogate.
noncollapse: Relative to declared futures; not intrinsic hidden meaning, intelligence, or fitness.

definition: A carrier coordinate updated on-kernel whose accepted source is generated by the system trajectory; a carried instrument satisfies the same condition for visibility, thresholds, and checks.
noncollapse: Physical location inside a boundary is insufficient for carriedness.

definition: A formed package plus carried instrument, carried ledger, and carried P1–P5 repair generator, with lawful occurrence separately requiring permission, ledger membership, admissibility, on-kernel realization, and re-audit.
noncollapse: An organism or agent is not thereby an E-system; P6 is governance, not a repair payload.

definition: A challenge history with complete audit inventory in which every repair occurrence is carried; external repair makes the history subsidized rather than self-repairing.
noncollapse: Choosing a larger carrier may change the verdict and must be declared.

definition: A finite probe catalog, carried active family, exposure budget, and allocation/acquisition/retirement moves; acquisition is strict only against same-family saturation.
noncollapse: Exposure is not free and selection is not licensed as an unqualified argmax.

definition: A low-dimensional carried quantity with a declared constraint, ledger, potential, or shadow-price role.
noncollapse: Correlation with outcomes makes a proxy, not a currency.

definition: A positive-semidefinite leftover measuring what a dissolving/target probe family sees beyond a native family under a declared audit energy.
noncollapse: Residuals are interface- and bridge-relative; exact adequacy is not generic.

definition: A localized obstruction or unresolved direction that survives the currently admitted probe family/budget.
noncollapse: Dissolution is framework-bound; not every obstruction is removable by ascent.

definition: A law whose statement quantifies over histories, horizons, moving covers, accumulated budgets, adversaries, or transport through time, rather than only static package structure.
noncollapse: G-laws must not be collapsed into static F-laws by dropping temporal hypotheses.

definition: A dependency cycle in which every rule capable of extending access or enabling a capability requires a premise available only after that extension/capability has already occurred.
noncollapse: Not yet a canonical SBT theorem in the supplied corpus; Step 3 must decide its exact carrier and fixed-point form.

definition: Four distinct statuses: stateable in the vocabulary; mechanism instantiated; attainable by a lawful path; observed within a declared horizon.
noncollapse: Existing SBT status machinery motivates this split but does not yet supply this exact four-way VII theorem.

definition: A proposed audited contact event/object between independently formed theory packages, with shared evaluation domain, source/provenance, compatibility, and an irreducibility or anti-product witness.
noncollapse: Must not be identified by fiat with repair join, categorical product, common refinement, common source, or message exchange.

definition: A proposed relation in which one package/event makes another formation reachable without necessarily causing, containing, determining, or descending to it.
noncollapse: Must be typed against causation, descent, sufficiency, and theorist/carrier/co-trigger attribution.
